abstract:
Abstract
                  The Artificial Social Agent Questionnaire (ASAQ) evaluates human interaction experiences with Artificial Social Agents (ASAs), including virtual agents, chatbots, and robots. Allowing researchers to make claims about its results depends on the validity of the questionnaire. Concurrent validity refers to the degree to which a questionnaire agrees with other established instruments that measure related constructs. To examine the concurrent validity of ASAQ, we used eight established questionnaires, including the Godspeed Questionnaire Series, the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology, and the Working Alliance Inventory. We selected these measures because of their conceptual overlap with ASAQ. A diverse sample of 666 participants evaluated ten agents they had recently interacted with using both the ASAQ and the established questionnaires. The results show moderate to high correlations for over 80% of ASAQ’s 24 constructs and dimensions, providing evidence for its concurrent validity. Our findings can help researchers judge whether the ASAQ is an appropriate and valid instrument to evaluate their social agent.

ur.tldr: 为检验人工社会智能体问卷（ASAQ）的同时效度，666 名参与者对 10 个智能体进行评价，将 ASAQ 与 Godspeed、UTAUT、工作联盟量表等 8 个成熟量表对比。结果显示 ASAQ 的 24 个构念与维度中超过 80% 呈中到高相关，验证了其作为评估人与人工社会智能体交互体验工具的可靠性。

title: Are you measuring what I am measuring? Concurrent validity of the Artificial Social Agent Questionnaire
